chunks: Al-Saffār narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from al-Kāhilī, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about madhy, and he said: “Whatever of it is accompanied by desire, then perform wudu (ablution) from it.”

And we understand this to mean that when it occurs in an unusual manner, because the customary and usual kind does not make repeating the wudu (ablution) obligatory, whether it comes out with desire or without desire; or the intent by it may be a type of recommendation.

And what indicates that is what al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me of: from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Saffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from more than one of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“There is no wudu (ablution) for madhy resulting from desire, nor from arousal, nor from kissing, nor from touching the private part, nor from lying together; and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it.”

key_terms.اَلْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid being discussed in the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Does madhy require wudu (ablution) or washing in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling on madhy and whether it necessitates wudu (ablution). The cited reports indicate that ordinary madhy does not invalidate wudu (ablution) and does not require washing the body or garment, while the earlier report is understood either in a restricted sense or as recommending wudu (ablution).
